A common application of matrix models is in formulation of conservation and management strategies for potentially at-risk populations.
This is known in some circles as

PVAs can take on various forms, but a common approach is to formulate a matrix model that projects whether a population is likely to increase or decrease, and what the effects of possible demographic changes might be.

For example, in the case of a harvested fish population, management strategies could include size/age restrictions, marine reserves, restrictions on fishing seasons, etc.
It is often far from clear what the impact of each of these strategies would be.
Still, it is necessary to estimate those impacts to formulate rational conservation strategies, particularly because there are typically severe costs and constraints in implementing them.
One approach to quantifying the impacts of a strategy is to estimate how it would change the coefficients in the matrix

This notation overlaps with others, including the notation for the matrix transpose. Unfortunately, there are few concise ways to indicate different operations in mathematics, so there notation is frequently reused for different purposes by different authors. Symbols must be interpreted on a case-by-case basis from the (hopefully) clear context.
